project: Namias Portfolio V1 — Complete Test Coverage & Functionality Completion
summary: Complete all remaining test coverage and resolve functionality gaps in Portfolio V1. Covers 40+ untested files across sections, UI components, hooks, lib utilities, section data fetchers, app routes, middleware, canary tokens, sanity, chat internal, and RAG internals. Adds component tests, integration tests, unit tests, and functionality hardening for streaming SSR, chat threading, smooth scroll, magic cursor, error boundary, contact modal, and monolithic home layout.
narrative: Portfolio V1 has 71 test files and strong coverage of API routes, chatbot core, RAG primitives, and the most complex UI components. However, a gap audit reveals 40+ files with zero test coverage. Some of these are trivial utilities (date.ts, constants.ts, utils.ts) but others are critical: the monolithic HomeContent layout, all 8 Skeleton components, the SectionProvider context, the Lenis smooth-scroll provider, MagicCursor cursor follower, ErrorBoundary, ContactModal, the SWR config, all 11 server-side section data fetchers, the root layout and providers, blog and project route pages, the request middleware, canary token routes, and the Sanity client. Several functionality gaps also exist: HomeContent is a monolithic file with no composable testing surface, streaming SSR has no dedicated test, chat threading UI (ThreadSidebar/ThreadToggle) lacks CRUD tests, Lenis and MagicCursor have no accessibility or behavior tests, ErrorBoundary and ContactModal lack error-state coverage, and none of the section data fetchers have unit tests for empty/error handling. This PRD defines a systematic plan to close every gap, organized by layer, with a verification phase that ensures tsc, eslint, vitest, and react-doctor all stay green.
principles: Every source file in src/ must have at least one test exercising its primary behavior or render path.
No test file may exceed 400 lines — split large coverage into focused files per component/module.

Existing uncovered bulk test files (sections-uncovered, ui-uncovered, hooks-uncovered) must be kept and extended, not replaced — new tests can be added to them or split into individual files as appropriate.
Feature-flag-aware: tests must verify both flag-on and flag-off states where applicable.
Accessibility-first: all component tests must verify keyboard navigation, focus management, and aria attributes where the component uses them.
Type-safe and tested: tsc, eslint, vitest, and react-doctor must all stay green after every epic.
One story slice per commit — test additions, functionality fixes, and verification are separate commits.
No comments in code — the only documentation is the PRD, the component name, and any JSDoc the type demands.

designDecisions.choice: Add new tests to the existing uncovered bulk files when the component is small and shares mocks. Create dedicated test files for complex components (HomeContent, HomeContentStreaming, ThreadSidebar, ErrorBoundary, ContactModal, MagicCursor).
designDecisions.rationale: Keeps PR diff small for trivial components while giving complex components their own test surface with focused mocks.

designDecisions.choice: Each of the 11 server.ts files gets a dedicated test file under src/__tests__/lib/sections/ that tests: (a) returns CMS data when fetch succeeds, (b) returns fallback data when fetch fails, (c) returns fallback data when CMS payload is empty.
designDecisions.rationale: These fetchers are the data backbone for every section. A single shared test pattern reduces boilerplate while ensuring consistent coverage.

designDecisions.choice: Test route pages as integration tests that render the page component with mocked child sections and data fetchers. Do NOT attempt full SSR rendering in Vitest (jsdom limitations).
designDecisions.rationale: Integration tests catch composition errors (wrong props, missing providers, broken layout nesting) without the complexity of a full SSR environment.

designDecisions.choice: Test LenisProvider by mocking the lenis library and verifying children render and prefers-reduced-motion disables smooth scroll. Test MagicCursor by verifying mouse-move event handlers update position state and touch devices hide the cursor.
designDecisions.rationale: These components wrap third-party libraries. Mock the library and test the React integration layer.

designDecisions.choice: Use a test harness component that throws on render inside the ErrorBoundary. Verify fallback UI renders with error message and retry button. Simulate retry by toggling a key prop to remount children.
designDecisions.rationale: ErrorBoundary cannot be tested with standard render + fireEvent because the error must be thrown during React commit phase. A dedicated harness is the standard React Testing Library pattern.

designDecisions.choice: Mock the form submission API call. Test: (a) renders form fields, (b) shows validation errors for empty fields, (c) shows validation error for invalid email, (d) calls onSubmit with form data on valid submission, (e) shows success message after submission, (f) shows error message on submission failure.
designDecisions.rationale: Form components are high-risk for regressions. Cover the full happy path and all error states.

designDecisions.choice: Mock the chat thread store. Test: (a) renders thread list from store, (b) clicking a thread selects it and updates URL, (c) create button dispatches create action, (d) delete button dispatches delete action with confirmation, (e) empty state shows 'No threads' message.
designDecisions.rationale: ThreadSidebar is the primary navigation UI for the chat feature. URL sync and CRUD operations must be verified.

designDecisions.choice: All 8 skeleton components share a common test pattern in a single file (src/__tests__/components/skeletons.test.tsx). Each test verifies: (a) renders without crashing, (b) contains the correct number of shimmer/animated blocks, (c) respects dark mode if applicable.
designDecisions.rationale: Skeletons are structurally simple. A shared test file with parameterized tests avoids 8 near-identical files.

designDecisions.choice: Mock NextRequest and NextResponse. Test that the middleware: (a) blocks requests with invalid content-type headers, (b) passes through requests with valid content-type headers, (c) passes through requests with no content-type header.
designDecisions.rationale: Middleware runs at the edge and is invisible to component tests. Unit tests with mocked request objects are the standard approach.

designDecisions.choice: Test canary route pages by: (a) verifying they render without crashing, (b) verifying they include the expected honeypot markers (hidden fields, decoy links), (c) verifying they do not leak any real application data or environment variables.
designDecisions.rationale: Canary routes are security-critical. Tests must confirm they behave as honeypots without exposing real data.

designDecisions.choice: Mock the @sanity/client module. Test that client.ts creates a configured Sanity client with the correct project ID, dataset, and API version. Test that live.ts creates a live client with the right configuration.
designDecisions.rationale: Sanity client configuration errors cause silent failures in production. Unit tests verify the configuration object matches expectations.

designDecisions.choice: Mirror the source directory structure under src/__tests__/. New test files go into: src/__tests__/lib/sections/, src/__tests__/lib/chat/, src/__tests__/lib/rag/, src/__tests__/app/blog/, src/__tests__/app/projects/, src/__tests__/middleware/, src/__tests__/sanity/, src/__tests__/canary/.
designDecisions.rationale: Mirroring the source structure makes it trivial to find the test file for any source file. This is the pattern already used by existing tests (src/__tests__/lib/, src/__tests__/hooks/, etc.).

epics.title: Functionality gaps
epics.summary: Address 11 functionality gaps: HomeContent streaming SSR, chat threading, Lenis smooth scroll, MagicCursor, ErrorBoundary, ContactModal, SWR config, section data fetcher error handling, SectionProvider config merging, and skeleton structural fidelity.

stories.title: Functionality: HomeContent section composition
stories.details: Verify that HomeContent renders all sections in the correct order and respects feature flags for conditional sections (BlogSection, ProjectsSectionRevamped). Already covered by test in S-2.2, but confirm the component actually handles all flag combinations correctly. If bugs are found during testing, fix them.

stories.title: Functionality: Streaming SSR Suspense boundaries
stories.details: Verify that HomeContentStreaming wraps each section in a Suspense boundary with the correct skeleton fallback. Test that all 5+ streaming sections have matching skeletons. If any section is missing its Suspense boundary or skeleton, add it.

stories.title: Functionality: Chat threading CRUD and persistence
stories.details: Verify ThreadSidebar creates, selects, and deletes threads correctly. Verify thread selection updates URL search params. Verify thread list persists across page navigation. If bugs are found (e.g., deleted thread still shows, URL not in sync), fix them.

stories.title: Functionality: Lenis smooth scroll prefers-reduced-motion
stories.details: Verify LenisProvider checks prefers-reduced-motion media query and disables smooth scroll when the user prefers reduced motion. If the check is missing, add it. Verify lenis.destroy() is called on unmount.

stories.title: Functionality: MagicCursor touch vs mouse detection
stories.details: Verify MagicCursor hides on touch devices and shows on mouse devices. Verify hover targets are correctly detected. Verify reduced-motion disables cursor animation. If touch detection is missing, add pointer media query check.

stories.title: Functionality: ErrorBoundary retry and logging
stories.details: Verify ErrorBoundary catches errors, renders fallback with error message, and retry button remounts children. If error logging is missing, add console.error in development. If retry does not reset error state, fix the key-based remount pattern.

stories.title: Functionality: ContactModal form validation and submission
stories.details: Verify ContactModal validates email format, name (non-empty), and message (non-empty). Verify error messages display inline. Verify submission calls API and shows success/error states. If validation rules are missing, add them.

stories.title: Functionality: SWR global config error handling
stories.details: Verify the SWR config provides error retry (max 3 attempts), dedup interval (2s+), and revalidate on focus. If any global config value is missing or incorrect, fix it.

stories.title: Functionality: Section data fetcher error resilience
stories.details: Verify all 11 section data fetchers return fallback data when CMS fetch fails or returns empty. Each fetcher must handle errors gracefully and never throw uncaught exceptions. If any fetcher lacks a try-catch or fallback, fix it.

stories.title: Functionality: SectionProvider config merging
stories.details: Verify SectionProvider merges default section order and visibility with overridden props. If merge logic is missing or incorrect (e.g., override replaces instead of merges), fix it.

stories.title: Functionality: Skeleton structural fidelity
stories.details: Verify each skeleton component renders the correct number of shimmer blocks that match the structure of its real section. If any skeleton is missing blocks (e.g., CertificationsSkeleton has 2 cert cards but real section shows 4), fix the skeleton.

epics.title: Verification
epics.summary: Run the full quality gate: typecheck, lint, all vitest tests, react-doctor, and dev server smoke test.

stories.title: Run tsc, eslint, vitest
stories.details: Run: npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint, npm run test -- --run. All must pass with the new tests included. Fix any type errors, lint violations, or test failures.

stories.title: Run react-doctor
stories.details: Run npm run doctor. Score must stay at 100/100. If a finding lands, fix it following the fix-react-doctor-finding skill.

stories.title: Dev server smoke test
stories.details: Run npm run dev and curl http://localhost:3000/. Verify the home page renders all sections. Curl /blog, /projects, and a few [slug] pages. Verify no console errors or hydration warnings.

stories.title: Update test count documentation
stories.details: Update the test count in AGENTS.md if it mentions a specific number. Update the scoreboard or testing documentation if applicable.

openQuestions: Should we split the existing sections-uncovered.test.tsx and ui-uncovered.test.tsx bulk files into individual per-component test files, or keep the bulk approach and just append new tests? The PRD currently plans to add to bulk files for small components and create dedicated files for complex ones.

Is there a way to reliably count 'files with test coverage' to track the primary success metric? Options: a custom vitest script, a find/grep approach, or a coverage report with file-level thresholds.
Should the canary token route tests be in the vite test suite (jsdom) or tested via a separate integration test? The PRD currently plans jsdom render tests since canary routes are simple React pages.

The legacy ProjectsSection (non-revamped) is tested through sections-uncovered.test.tsx but the revamped version has its own test file. Should we add a test that verifies IS_PROJECTS_REVAMP_ENABLED=false correctly falls back to the legacy ProjectsSection?

HomeContentStreaming uses Suspense boundaries that are difficult to test with jsdom + React 18. Should we add a note that these tests may need React 18's act() with fake timers, or defer to a future React 19 upgrade for better Suspense testing?

Some lib utilities (constants.ts, media-constants.ts, site-config.ts) are essentially static config files. Should their tests be simple snapshot tests or value-assertion tests? The PRD plans value-assertion tests for correctness.
Should we add a CI check that fails if the test count decreases? This would prevent regressions in coverage. Could be a GitHub Actions step that compares test count to a baseline.
